transcript.customer: Not a complaint for once! My monstera from last month has two big yellow leaves and I'm scared I'm killing it.
transcript.agent: You’re probably not killing it. Yellow monstera leaves are most often from overwatering—let the soil dry about 2 inches down before watering again, and make sure the pot drains well. You can remove the fully yellow leaves; they won’t turn green again.

transcript.customer: hi! yeah I'm a chronic overparent, I think I fuss too much
transcript.agent: That’s very relatable—most monsteras do better with a little benign neglect. Check the soil before watering, and wait until the top couple inches are dry; bright, indirect light and good drainage will do the rest.

transcript.customer: I water it every two days, it's in a bright room but no direct sun.
transcript.agent: Every two days is likely more often than it needs, especially if the soil is still moist below the surface. Let the top ~2 inches dry out before watering again, then water thoroughly and let excess drain away. Bright, indirect light sounds ideal.

transcript.customer: every two days, yeah. is that too much? it FELT like a lot but the internet is full of contradictory people
transcript.agent: For most monsteras, yes—every two days is usually too frequent. Let the top 2 inches of soil dry before watering; depending on your home, that may be closer to every 1–2 weeks. Bright indirect light is great, so you’re on the right track.

transcript.customer: Ohhh ok. So less water. How do I actually tell when it's ready then, do I just guess?
transcript.agent:
No guessing needed: stick a finger about 2 inches into the soil. If it feels dry there, it’s time to water; if it’s still cool or damp, wait a few more days and check again.

When you do water, soak the soil evenly until a little runs out of the drainage hole, then empty any saucer so the roots aren’t sitting in water.

transcript.customer: finger two inches down, got it. and Should I cut the yellow leaves off or leave them?
transcript.agent: You can remove them once they’re fully yellow—they won’t turn green again. Use clean scissors or pruners and cut the leaf stem close to the main stem without nicking it.

transcript.customer: ok cool. one more â€” it leans hard toward the window, is that bad or just dramatic
transcript.agent: Just dramatic—and normal. It’s reaching toward the light. Rotate the pot about a quarter turn every week or two so it grows more evenly.

transcript.customer: rotate it, love that. ok I feel much better
transcript.agent: Glad to hear it—your monstera sounds like it has a very attentive plant parent.

transcript.customer: You've saved a life today. Thank you!
transcript.agent: You’re very welcome—wishing your monstera a speedy return to its lush, less-yellow era.
